PullRequest.Title: Canvases: preserve focus on provider recovery
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #345309

## Motivation

A canvas can become available automatically after its provider is installed or recovers. That background presentation should not interrupt the user’s current modal workflow by closing Agent Customizations. Explicit user reveals and fresh successful `open_canvas` requests should continue to foreground the canvas normally.

## Change

Automatic canvas presentation uses a dedicated preserve-focus options path while a modal editor is active. Working-set restore remains responsible for restore group selection and editor-part suppression, so modal safety does not relocate an existing canvas tab. Running model requests wait for success, and a request that succeeds during an in-flight modal-safe open gets one foreground retry. The request projection distinguishes pending calls from failed, cancelled, or hydrated historical calls so only live intent bypasses modal preservation.

## Benefit

Users can finish installing or managing customizations without losing the modal, while intentional canvas opens remain immediate and predictable. The implementation reuses existing editor-service behavior and adds only the request-state distinction needed to preserve current semantics.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/canvases/test/common/agentHostCanvas.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/canvases/test/electron-browser/canvasService.test.ts` — 28 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/services/editor/test/browser/modalEditorGroup.test.ts --grep "findGroup keeps modal open when preserveFocus is true"` — 1 passing
- `npm run eslint -- <changed TypeScript files>` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- Live Code OSS Agents window: opened Agent Customizations, invoked the real CanvasService modal-safe presentation path, and verified `modalBefore: true`, `modalOpen: true`, with the canvas inactive behind the modal — passed

*🤖 Written by GitHub Copilot on behalf of @jruales.*

Scenarios.Scenario: A canvas provider recovers or publishes a canvas while Agent Customizations (a modal editor) is active.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The canvas/context observable reruns CanvasService's reconciliation, checks modal state, creates/reuses one CanvasInput, and calls editorService.openEditor. The modal-safe options preserve the modal. If the selected editor group already has an active editor, the inactive open updates only the tab/model; if it is empty, editor pane setup can continue into CanvasEditor model resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an external browser view when CanvasEditor becomes active and no presentation model/modelPromise exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold creation per canvas presentation/source; modelPromise coalesces concurrent resolution and presentation.model serves warm reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Automatic presentation already called editorService.openEditor and could create/load the same browser model; the diff changes focus/activation options rather than adding model creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only on the critical path when the supposedly inactive editor must become active because the target group is empty; otherwise model creation is deferred until activation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the canvas source URL in the external browser model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold URL load per new canvas presentation/source, with subsequent reveals reusing the retained model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same URL was loaded by the pre-diff foreground automatic open, generally earlier and with modal interruption.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Follows cold model creation; inactive tab-only presentation keeps it off the immediate path when the target group is nonempty.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible contexts and canvases scanned by the reconciliation autorun; actual boundary cardinality is one cold browser model per presented canvas/source.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Eligible canvases can still begin independent opens concurrently as before; each CanvasInput is coalesced by the opening map, and browser model creation is coalesced by modelPromise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold presentations may create one browser view and load one URL. Warm presentations reuse presentation.model; simultaneous cold resolves reuse modelPromise. Source changes invalidate and dispose the model.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: editorGroupView explicitly skips pane opening for inactive editors except when the group is empty, and CanvasService has direct model/modelPromise reuse.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A target group may be empty or nonempty, controlling whether an inactive open eagerly instantiates the editor pane, but either branch existed before and does not increase cold boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change preserves or defers existing editor/browser work while preventing modal focus loss.

Scenarios.Scenario: A live open_canvas tool call is running and then succeeds while a modal editor is active.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat-state projection scans backward for the latest request per live canvas. While request.pending is true, modal reconciliation skips presentation. On success, one foreground editor open proceeds; its cold browser creation/load is the same boundary as before but delayed until success.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an external browser view for the successfully opened canvas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per cold presentation/source after success; no call while the request remains pending under a modal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, canvas availability during a running call could immediately open and create the view; the diff delays that existing operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the successful foreground reveal's critical path, not on the running-request path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Navigate the external browser view to the canvas source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold load after success, cached for later reveals.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same load occurred on the earlier automatic presentation path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of cold canvas activation after the tool reports success.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Chat turns/response parts scanned until requests have been found for all live canvas instance IDs, plus the number of visible canvases reconciled. The new pending field adds only request-state discrimination, not an additional per-token boundary.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A given input has at most one open in flight. The pending gate suppresses rather than adds concurrency; successful opens for distinct canvases remain independently concurrent as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The derived request map suppresses unchanged outputs including pending state. Browser model cold/warm behavior remains one modelPromise/model per presentation/source.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: request state, modal gate, and open/model coalescing are explicit in the changed and transitive code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Chat history length varies, but the backward projection and its collection scan predate the diff; only a bounded Running-to-terminal output transition is newly distinguished.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed path removes eager work while pending and performs the existing single cold open after success.

Scenarios.Scenario: A fresh successful model request arrives while a modal-safe automatic editor open for the same canvas is still in flight.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first preserve-focus open completes, openInput's finally removes the opening marker and retriggers reconciliation, then a foreground retry opens the same CanvasInput. The retry is intentionally serialized after the first operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call editorService.openEditor twice for the same CanvasInput: first inactive/preserve-focus, then foreground.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two editor opens for one canvas in the specific overlap race; no concurrent duplicate because opening serializes them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Pre-diff automatic presentation used one foreground editor open and closed/interrupted the modal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The second call is needed to honor fresh foreground intent after the background open; it adds editor bookkeeping/activation after the first open completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the canvas browser model if the first or second editor activation needs it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Still one cold IPC creation, not two: both opens share one CanvasInput/presentation and resolveCanvasModel reuses modelPromise/model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The single pre-diff foreground open created the same one model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold creation/load occurs at the first actual CanvasEditor activation; the serialized retry does not duplicate it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold URL load for the shared presentation/source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The pre-diff foreground open loaded the URL once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold canvas activation waits for the load; the retry reuses it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One overlap per canvas/request completion. Cost does not multiply with chat updates because presentation.requestId acknowledges the request and pendingRequests is cleared.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Strictly serialized per CanvasInput by the opening map and pending.value.then retry. Distinct canvases retain pre-existing independent concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold first activation uses modelPromise; a second activation during/after creation reuses that promise/model. Warm opens perform no browser creation or URL reload.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the test asserts exactly two editor calls in the overlap, while source code proves serialization and browser-model reuse.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Editor-service bookkeeping cost depends on group state, but the heavyweight IPC/network boundaries are provably coalesced and the race is bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff adds one bounded editor activation call in a narrow race, but does not duplicate heavyweight browser creation/network work and preserves required foreground semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: The user explicitly reveals a canvas while a modal editor is active, including after a background tab-only presentation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: revealCanvas validates working-set restore and owner/source eligibility, reuses the CanvasInput, and calls openInput with preserveFocus false. If a preserve-focus open is in flight, the explicit reveal is sequenced after it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an external browser view on first canvas activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold creation per presentation/source, reused on subsequent explicit reveals.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Explicit reveal already made one foreground open and resolved the same model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold reveal waits for model creation and URL loading; warm reveal uses retained model.
On the cold explicit reveal path only.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected canvas; no collection fan-out from explicit reveal.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-input opens are coalesced; a stronger foreground request is sequenced after an in-flight preserve-focus request. No duplicate model creation occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm reveal reuses CanvasInput and retained browser model; cold reveal uses modelPromise coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from direct revealCanvas/openInput and resolveCanvasModel traces.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the mechanism; editor group placement may replace a move with an open, as before.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Foreground behavior and boundary cardinality are preserved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Working-set restore or ordinary canvas open completes and reconciliation runs after open completion.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: doOpenInput updates presentation state and triggers reconciliation; the new finally block deletes the opening marker and triggers another reconciliation. Each pass scans contexts/canvases and in-memory presentation maps, with no boundary calls when the presentation is already acknowledged.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional O(number of contexts + canvases + presentations/requests) in-memory scan per completed open. Opens are infrequent lifecycle events rather than frame/input events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The signal-driven scans are synchronous/reactive and serialized; the extra completion pass cannot start another open for an acknowledged normal/restore request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache miss or boundary is introduced; existing presentation/request state causes the completion scan to short-circuit each canvas.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the extra scan exists; low evidence that its bounded in-memory cost is a concrete regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large live canvas collections could increase CPU cost, but expected collection sizes and event frequency are limited, and there is no evidence of user-visible latency or repeated hot-path execution.
Scenarios.Verdict: Not reportable under the performance evidence standard. The extra scan is bounded to open completion and supports the race retry; no realistic hot/scaling impact is established.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. Traced modal-safe automatic presentation, running/successful model requests, the in-flight foreground retry, explicit reveal, and working-set completion through editor, IPC, and network boundaries. The only new repeated operations are a bounded serialized editor retry in one overlap race and one extra in-memory reconciliation scan per open completion; heavyweight browser-view creation and URL loading remain coalesced to one per presentation/source. No actionable performance finding met the reporting threshold.
